steps.title: Open the dashboard
steps.narration: Let's start at Trendora's home dashboard, where traders get their first look at the market each day.
steps.point_out: A green status badge in the corner confirms the backend is up and ready to serve real data.

steps.title: Check the Data Manager's storage footprint
steps.narration: From the sidebar we head into the Data Manager, which now shows exactly how much data the platform is holding.
steps.point_out: Right below the existing dataset numbers, a brand-new Storage footprint card shows the database's file size plus the price-bar, scanner-result, and forward-return counts it holds.

steps.title: Browse the stock leaderboard
steps.narration: Next stop is the stock leaderboard, where hundreds of companies are ranked side by side on the same scores.
steps.point_out: Each row carries its own leadership, entry-quality, risk, and setup scores.

steps.title: Search for Apple (AAPL)
steps.narration: Typing a ticker into the search box instantly narrows hundreds of rows down to the one we want.
steps.point_out: AAPL's row shows its sector and its "Megacap Leaders" theme alongside its scores.

steps.title: Open AAPL's own page
steps.narration: Clicking straight into AAPL's detail page confirms it tells the exact same story as the leaderboard row.
steps.point_out: The leadership score reads 55.78, matching the leaderboard exactly, with no discrepancy between the two views.

steps.title: Switch to the full price history
steps.narration: Toggling the chart from Recent to Full history pulls up decades of price action for the same stock.
steps.point_out: The chart redraws with far more history, and a small note explains the older bars are weekly-sampled to keep the chart readable.

steps.title: Back to the Data Manager
steps.narration: Returning to the Data Manager confirms the same storage numbers we saw earlier haven't drifted.
steps.point_out: The Storage footprint figures read exactly the same as before, even after browsing elsewhere.

steps.title: Test the job form with a bad date
steps.narration: We try entering a nonsense date into the data-job form to make sure it still catches the mistake.
steps.point_out: A clear red message flags the invalid date, and the Start button stays disabled until it's corrected.

expect.text: Enter a valid date as yyyy-MM-dd

steps.title: Peek at the watchlist
steps.narration: A quick stop at the watchlist shows the names being tracked, each still carrying its trusted scores.
steps.point_out: Saved tickers appear here with the reason they were added, alongside the same scores shown on the leaderboard.

steps.title: Visit the evidence ledger
steps.narration: Last stop is the evidence ledger, the audit trail behind every trading idea this product has tested.
steps.point_out: Every idea's real, out-of-sample track record lives here, so nothing is ever called proven unless it actually earned that label.
